issues.summary: Tiers and apps are put into the flat list_presets() namespace and fenced off by content refusals; the bundled tier presets have two incompatible homes; success criteria assert results on calls the plan says raise

evidence.detail: list_presets() is a flat iterdir() over presets/*.yml; it is the single writer behind `osprey init --list-presets` (init_cmd.py:1159-1171), `osprey profile presets` (profile_cmd.py:74-93, docstring 'Every name printed here is usable as osprey init --preset NAME', docs cli.rst:112,315) and four 'Unknown preset … Available:' messages. A presets/tiers/ subfolder is never listed, yet the criterion says list_presets() returns the five 'plus the three tiers'. `osprey profile card --preset control-assistant-readwrite` names a flag the card verb does not have (profile_cmd.py:139-147) and a preset the plan deletes. `resolve_build_profile(None,'logbook')` is the call path FR4 refuses (build_profile_resolve.py:493-516), and even unrefused it cannot list `graph`: `_renders_graphdb_block` (build_profile_model.py:876) is True only when the profile's own config/services spell graphdb, which FR4 forbids an app preset to carry. `osprey build --preset readonly` on an extends-less tier layer renders an empty agent with no message (build_cmd.py:4175). profile_cmd.py `_off_chain_problem` (1077) and the `_preset_data_names` bundle comparison (1321-1378) refuse every extends-less tier and every app preset at `osprey init`, so FR10 cannot emit them as written. Pin tables (test_preset_hash_pin.py:340, test_hook_selection_pins.py:82, test_preset_dependency_pin.py:85) and test_build_preset.py:788 iterate list_presets() and would build the apps standalone.

'Location is the type' on BOTH sides. Package ships presets/{control-assistant,hello-world}.yml, presets/tiers/{readonly,readwrite,admin}.yml, presets/apps/{logbook,knowledge,channel-finder}.yml. `list_presets()` keeps its contract (deployments only); add `list_tiers()` and `list_apps()` beside it; `osprey profile presets` prints three headed blocks; pin tables iterate the three listings (hash/hook/dependency pins resolve, they do not build); test_each_bundled_preset_builds_clean iterates deployments only. One kind-keyed refusal in resolve_build_profile and osprey init: ' is a tier/app, not a deployment. Rewrite criteria: list_presets()==[control-assistant, hello-world]; list_apps()==[channel-finder, knowledge, logbook]; list_tiers()==[admin, readonly, readwrite]; `osprey build --preset logbook` and `--preset readonly` refuse with the message; in a repo from `osprey init --preset control-assistant`, the composed render build/

issues.summary: FR3's app composition is a splice: the whole host config (armed writes, every enabled server) underlies the app so logbook.yml must re-carry today's 11 negations; a new `preset:` key and a third 'replace' merge semantic duplicate `extends:`+deep-merge; attachment is derived from location for apps but spelled in content for tiers; 20+ profile keys are unassigned; the data bundle falls to a constant

evidence.detail: Host spells control_system.writes_enabled: true (238), servers.bluesky/health enabled (449-450); registry/mcp.py:1427-1440 enables every framework server unless `enabled: false`; control-assistant-logbook.yml carries 11 `*.enabled: false`/writes false keys to narrow the host — FR3 reproduces that carve-down inside logbook.yml. channel-finder-standalone.yml sets no writes key and no writes-check hook, so as an app on `access: any` it inherits writes_enabled: true for every roster member. `_deep_merge` (build_profile_merge.py:58) with list union is the ONE layer rule for extends, overlays and persona deltas; FR3 adds `preset:` (not in _KNOWN_PROFILE_KEYS, build_profile_load.py:174, so `osprey validate apps/logbook.yml` and `osprey set` refuse it) plus a replace semantic plus a refusal of `extends:`, while `_resolve_extends` (build_profile_merge.py:362,418) already resolves a bundled preset name. If config lists replace, the knowledge render loses the host floor deny `mcp__osprey_workspace__setup_patch` (control-assistant.yml:760) and gets the admin-only tool behind `ask`. deploy_services is read raw (build_profile_load.py:1585); the three tier presets hand-spell deploy_services: false, modules.web_terminals.enabled: false and ~25 comment lines each; the five persona presets pin web_terminals.enabled: false by hand or the render hosts a second web tier (build_profile_emit.py:789). BuildProfile has 30+ top-level fields (provider, model, mcp_servers, data, env, deploy, dispatch, …) FR3 never assigns; ariel-standalone.yml:21 spells provider: anthropic. preset_data_bundle (build_profile_presets.py:208) walks extends for app_template and returns DEFAULT_DATA_BUNDLE='control_assistant' for a chain naming none — right by coincidence.

issues.fix: One resolver rule. `resolve_profile_document` returns kind ∈ {root, tier, app} from location (operator tiers/ and apps/; bundled presets/tiers/ and presets/apps/). Base = resolved root (tier) or `_resolve_extends` of the named app preset (app: the file spells `extends: logbook`; no `preset:` key; an app file whose extends names a deployment or tier is refused). Result = `_deep_merge(base, layer)` for both kinds — one list rule, union. For an app the config is `_deep_merge(_deep_merge(host_facts, app_preset.config), app_file.config)` where host_facts = the host's config MINUS `claude_code.servers.*` and MINUS every `control_system.*writes_enabled` key (claude_code.permissions.* is KEPT and unioned, so the host floor deny survives); the composer then pins `control_system.writes_enabled: false` and every `control_system.connector.<type>.writes_enabled: false` structurally on every app render, and adds `writes-check` to hooks — apps never write to the machine (lint error `web_terminals.app_render_writes_enabled` as the guard). Every other top-level key (provider, model, mcp_servers, data, env, deploy, dispatch, …) is taken verbatim from the host; the data bundle and provenance are the host's, and preset_data_bundle(<app>) raises. Attachment is a fact of the kind for BOTH tiers and apps: the resolver sets deploy_services=False, services={}, modules.web_terminals.enabled=false and refuses those keys when spelled in a tier/app file. Key set per kind: tier → root keys minus {extends, data, project_name, deploy, services, lifecycle, env, environment, dependencies, exclude} plus {extra_mounts, seed_base, image}; app → {extends, name, hooks, rules, skills, agents, output_styles, web_panels, default_panel, claude_md_template, channel_finder_mode, config, mcp_servers, extra_mounts, seed_base, image}; loader, `osprey set` and `osprey validate <file>` use the kind's set. App presets list only what they ARE (lists, brief, panels, `servers.<x>.enabled: true` for off-by-default servers, which host servers they switch off — osprey_facility_knowledge included — as a stated decision); bundled tier layers shrink to their real content (writes pins, web.ui_mode, panels/skills/privilege lifts). Tests: composed knowledge render denies both setup_patch and draft_concept; composed logbook render has emits_persona_profiles False, host provider, every writes_enabled false, no bluesky/health/controls/python server; an app file spelling provider: or deploy_services: is refused.

alternativeApproach: One resolver rule, one bundled layout, one card list, one migration. (1) 'Location is the type' on both sides: operator tiers/ and apps/ beside profile.yml, bundled presets/tiers/ and presets/apps/; three listings, one kind-keyed refusal for init/build/validate/set. (2) One merge: _deep_merge over a kind-chosen base (root for a tier, the extends-named app preset for an app); for apps the config is underlaid with the host's deployment facts only and writes are pinned off structurally; attachment is a fact of the kind, never spelled; no exclude in tiers or apps. (3) One roster helper is the only place that knows an app card exists; derived entries live in memory, typed, never written back; one title on every surface; apps are a landing group type. (4) The build projects one derived `renders` catalog; folder + file are the source. (5) dispatch.tier is one more reference to a tier: one image producer in both image modes, one build step on both deploy paths, the worker runs the baked tier config from one project dir; the flagship preset defaults the chat-reachable worker to readonly. (6) The rename is a schema migration: per-document key normalisation at the single parse point, `osprey init --revalidate` as the rewrite, schema floor bumped, window end enforced by a test; rendered configs carry new spellings only and an old render is refused as drift. (7) The config-key guard models two roots + three apps composed over the host. (8) Scope equals the criterion: 80-file deletion checklist, every docs/plugin/template mention, brief-template renames, `scaffold tiers`, and an internal-vocabulary phase.
